entries.answer: I call the customer twice and send a message on the app. While waiting I ask the security guard or a neighbour politely about the flat. I check the map pin and landmark again. If still no answer after 10 minutes, I inform the dispatcher, mark it in the app as customer not reachable, and tell the customer by message that we'll reattempt tomorrow.
I will drive fast before the rain becomes heavy and finish all 8 quickly, talking to customers on phone while riding.
Don't hand it over as if nothing's wrong. Snap a few photos of the box, flag it to the hub and get it noted on the app. Then follow whatever they say — return it or deliver with a remark.
I will call customer 2-3 times and ask nearby shop wala bhaiya about the address. If not found i will call to office and return the parcel.

I slow down and wear my raincoat, and keep the parcels covered in plastic. I re-plan the route to avoid flooded roads and do the nearest drops first. I message customers that there may be a delay and update the dispatcher. If it gets too heavy I stop under a shelter for a while; safety is more important than the target.
I will deliver it, not my problem.
Call the customer.
I will manage my time properly and do the needful.

First I check I'm at the right location using the map and landmark. I call the customer and send an SMS, and wait about 10 minutes. I politely ask the guard or neighbours if they know the person. If I still can't reach them I call support, follow their process for reattempt, and mark the reason in the app.
I will leave the parcel outside the gate and mark it delivered.
I will call the customer and wait for some time.
Ring them a couple of times and drop a text. Ask around — the watchman usually knows who lives where. If nobody turns up, get in touch with the dispatcher and take it back for another try.
Customer, call, wait, polite, address, map, support.
I will try calling, if no pick up then i will ask watchman uncle. Still no then i will message customer and come back next day.
I have my own bike and driving licence since 2019.

I put on my raincoat and cover the parcels. I check the map and plan a route that avoids water-logged roads, doing the closest deliveries first. I ride slowly with headlights on and never use the phone while riding — I stop to call customers and tell them I may be 20–30 minutes late. I update the dispatcher about the delay.
Rain doesn't matter, I will ride at the same speed and go through the water, target must be completed.
I will drive slowly and carefully in the rain.
Take it easy on the throttle and stay off the flooded streets. Sort the drops so the nearby ones happen first, and give the customers a heads-up that I'm running behind.
Rain time i will not rush. First nearby deliveries i will do, and inform customers delay will be there. Raincoat and parcel cover i will use.
Drive slowly.
I will wait for rain to stop and then deliver.
I will plan properly and handle the situation.

I don't take it as normal. I take photos of the damage from all sides, inform the hub supervisor before leaving, and mark it as damaged in the app. If they tell me to deliver, I show the customer the damage and let them decide to accept or refuse, and note their decision.
I will tape it so it looks okay and deliver it, nobody will know.
I will tell the supervisor that the parcel is damaged.
Get pictures of the dented corner, let the warehouse in-charge know and log it before I leave with it.
Damaged parcel i will not take. I will show to hub incharge and take photo, then they will give new parcel or note it.
Photo, report, damage, supervisor, app, honest.
I am a fast driver and I know all roads in Bangalore.
